subject: Make cross-carrier disagreement a first-class EvidenceGraph protocol, not last-writer-wins

law: Every receipt must bind observer/provider, worktree/repo identity where local state matters, source commit/input digests, and observation time sufficiently to explain disagreement.
When two valid receipts assert incompatible facts about the same claim, EvidenceGraph creates TraceDivergence and a reconciliation obligation; neither claim silently overwrites the other.
Reconciliation compares scope first: current-live vs historical, primary worktree vs side worktree, immutable commit vs moving branch, provider observation vs semantic completion.
Resolution emits one of: superseded_observation, scope_separated, stale_factor, true_regression, or unresolved. Preserve both original receipts.
A resolved disagreement should produce KnownNonCause and RegressionFence so future ContextCompiler capsules carry the reason the losing explanation was rejected.
Use cross-provider review when possible; the provider that authored one side should not be the sole resolver.
